question.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y=-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=-1$ and ${\mu }_{2}=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}] \\  & =-3\text{E}[{X}_{1}]+2\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & =-3\cdot {\mu }_{1}+2\cdot {\mu }_{2} \\  & =-3\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 4 \\  & =3+8 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=5,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=3,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}] \\  & =(-3)^{2}\cdot 5+{2}^{2}\cdot 3+2\cdot (-3)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =45+12-24 \\  & =33.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(11,33).
$$
